capabilities.title: VirtualBox
capabilities.description: VirtualBox is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Install the current supported Windows host package and extension components only from the official site.
Official download or account page: https://www.virtualbox.org/wiki/Downloads

capabilities.title: Ubuntu Desktop VM
capabilities.description: Ubuntu Desktop VM is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Download a supported Ubuntu LTS desktop image and install it as a VirtualBox guest.
Official download or account page: https://ubuntu.com/download/desktop
verification: Boot Ubuntu, sign in, open Terminal, and create a shared learner folder.

capabilities.title: DOSBox in Ubuntu
capabilities.description: DOSBox in Ubuntu is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Install DOSBox from Ubuntu packages inside the Ubuntu guest.
Official download or account page: https://help.ubuntu.com/community/DOSBox
verification: Launch DOSBox and mount the learner folder without exposing the host drive root.

capabilities.title: Licensed Microsoft QBasic media
capabilities.description: Licensed Microsoft QBasic media is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Use learner-owned MS-DOS 5/6 or Windows 95/98 media containing QBasic. XcelerateAI does not provide, mirror, or link to proprietary binaries.
verification: Mount the licensed files and launch QBASIC.EXE in DOSBox.

capabilities.title: Git for Windows
capabilities.description: Git for Windows is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Install Git, keep the recommended beginner defaults, then configure your name and email.
Official download or account page: https://git-scm.com/download/win
verification: Run git --version, git config user.name, and git config user.email.

capabilities.title: GitHub account
capabilities.description: GitHub account is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Create or reuse a personal GitHub account and configure account recovery.
Official download or account page: https://github.com/signup
verification: Create a private practice repository, connect a local repository, and push one commit.

weeks.title: Editor, Statements, and Output
weeks.outcome: Build, debug, explain, and verify a labelled arithmetic program.

study.objective: Learn and actively rehearse statement, variable, numeric expression, string, comment so you can explain, select, debug, and apply them while creating a labelled arithmetic program.

resources.purpose: Learn the exact definitions, applications, and mistakes assessed by the Week 1 Skill Check, then preview the a labelled arithmetic program contract.
Rehearse the same five weekly concepts through prediction, error recognition, and explanation without affecting progression.

skillCheck.title: Editor, Statements, and Output Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 1 guide defines statement. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: numbers and operators producing a value

questions.explanation: statement means a QBASIC instruction; it is used to use PRINT to show a result. Avoid this mistake: type prose as executable code.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to use PRINT to show a result. Which concept from the Week 1 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: statement is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to type prose as executable code.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for variable, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: expect text input to behave as a number
omit the string suffix in traditional QBASIC examples
use spaces in a variable name

questions.explanation: variable means a named storage location; it is used to store TOTAL before printing. Avoid this mistake: use spaces in a variable name.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to use spaces in a variable name. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: variable is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use spaces in a variable name.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 1 guide correctly demonstrates numeric expression?

options.label: use PRINT to show a result

questions.explanation: numeric expression means numbers and operators producing a value; it is used to calculate PRICE * QUANTITY. Avoid this mistake: expect text input to behave as a number.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: calculate PRICE * QUANTITY?
questions.explanation: numeric expression is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect text input to behave as a number.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain string before coding. Which explanation is accurate?
questions.explanation: string means text data; it is used to store NAME$. Avoid this mistake: omit the string suffix in traditional QBASIC examples.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "text data". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: string is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to omit the string suffix in traditional QBASIC examples.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that comment was misunderstood?

options.label: use spaces in a variable name
expect text input to behave as a number

questions.explanation: comment means a note ignored during execution; it is used to use REM to explain intent. Avoid this mistake: comment out required behavior.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—comment out required behavior—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: comment is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to comment out required behavior.

builds.title: Microbuild: a labelled arithmetic program
builds.outcome: A working, tested a labelled arithmetic program.
builds.brief: Deliverable: a labelled arithmetic program. Required behavior: demonstrate statement, variable, numeric expression, string, comment; complete one normal, one boundary, and one invalid case; and keep a short expected-versus-actual test record. Evidence: the exact run command, the repaired defect, the three final results, and an honest README.

steps.text: Write a three-case contract for a labelled arithmetic program: one normal case, one boundary case, and one invalid case. For each, record the input or action and the expected result before coding.
Create the runnable source and implement the normal case first. Make statement, variable, numeric expression visible in the code or interface, then run the exact launch command once.

Add the boundary and invalid-case behavior using string and comment. Deliberately reproduce this weekly mistake—comment out required behavior—record the symptom, repair one cause, and rerun the same case.
Run all three contract cases again. In README, record the environment, exact run command, expected versus actual results, repaired defect, and one known limit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A learner can follow the README command and run a labelled arithmetic program through its stated normal case without an unexplained error.
The finished work visibly demonstrates the Week 1 concepts: statement, variable, numeric expression, string, comment.
The test record lists normal, boundary, and invalid inputs or actions with both expected and actual results.
The debugging note names the failing case, observed symptom, root cause, single repair, successful rerun, and one known limit.

hints: If the normal case fails, reduce it to the smallest input or action involving statement and inspect the observed value before editing.
If the boundary or invalid case fails, revisit the guide warning "comment out required behavior" and change one cause at a time.

study.objective: Learn and actively rehearse INPUT, IF block, comparison, boolean operator, branch order so you can explain, select, debug, and apply them while creating a grade or fare adviser.

resources.purpose: Learn the exact definitions, applications, and mistakes assessed by the Week 2 Skill Check, then preview the a grade or fare adviser contract.
Rehearse the same five weekly concepts through prediction, error recognition, and explanation without affecting progression.

skillCheck.title: Input and Decisions Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 2 guide defines INPUT. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: reads a value from the learner

questions.explanation: INPUT means reads a value from the learner; it is used to use INPUT "Age"; AGE. Avoid this mistake: expect INPUT to validate every value.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to use INPUT "Age"; AGE. Which concept from the Week 2 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: INPUT is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect INPUT to validate every value.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for IF block, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: forget END IF for a block form

questions.explanation: IF block means conditional execution; it is used to use IF...THEN...ELSE. Avoid this mistake: forget END IF for a block form.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to forget END IF for a block form. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: IF block is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to forget END IF for a block form.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 2 guide correctly demonstrates comparison?

options.label: use AND for a bounded range

questions.explanation: comparison means a true-or-false relationship; it is used to check SCORE >= 50. Avoid this mistake: use an impossible overlapping range.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: check SCORE >= 50?
questions.explanation: comparison is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use an impossible overlapping range.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain boolean operator before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: reads a value from the learner

questions.explanation: boolean operator means combines conditions; it is used to use AND for a bounded range. Avoid this mistake: replace AND with a comma.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "combines conditions". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: boolean operator is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to replace AND with a comma.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that branch order was misunderstood?

options.label: expect INPUT to validate every value
forget END IF for a block form

questions.explanation: branch order means the sequence conditions are tested; it is used to test highest grade threshold first. Avoid this mistake: put the broadest condition first.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—put the broadest condition first—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: branch order is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to put the broadest condition first.

skillCheck.title: Loops and Counters Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 3 guide defines FOR loop. Which description matches that definition?
questions.explanation: FOR loop means counted repetition; it is used to use FOR I = 1 TO 10. Avoid this mistake: forget NEXT.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to use FOR I = 1 TO 10. Which concept from the Week 3 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: FOR loop is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to forget NEXT.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for DO loop, which warning identifies the error to avoid?
questions.explanation: DO loop means condition-controlled repetition; it is used to repeat a menu until quit. Avoid this mistake: omit an exit condition.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to omit an exit condition. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: DO loop is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to omit an exit condition.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 3 guide correctly demonstrates counter?
questions.explanation: counter means tracks event count; it is used to increment VALIDCOUNT. Avoid this mistake: reset it inside the loop.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: increment VALIDCOUNT?
questions.explanation: counter is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to reset it inside the loop.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain accumulator before coding. Which explanation is accurate?
questions.explanation: accumulator means stores a running result; it is used to add SCORE to TOTAL. Avoid this mistake: leave it uninitialized conceptually.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "stores a running result". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: accumulator is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to leave it uninitialized conceptually.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that trace table was misunderstood?
questions.explanation: trace table means records changing values per iteration; it is used to trace I and TOTAL. Avoid this mistake: guess the final result.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—guess the final result—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: trace table is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to guess the final result.

skillCheck.title: SUBs and FUNCTIONs Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 4 guide defines SUB. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: a named calculation returning a value
a named procedure without a returned expression value

questions.explanation: SUB means a named procedure without a returned expression value; it is used to call a display procedure. Avoid this mistake: use it when a calculation result is needed by callers.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to call a display procedure. Which concept from the Week 4 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: SUB is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use it when a calculation result is needed by callers.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for FUNCTION, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: forget to assign the function name
expect it in the main program
